Reuse of public sector information is the use also for commercial or non-commercial purposes other than the original purpose for which it was created within the powers or functions of a public sector organization. The provision of public sector information to a public sector organization in connection with the exercise of its powers or functions is not reuse within the meaning of Access to Public Information Act. question:
Do you have a definition of open data reuse in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please specify it.
ground_truth_explanation:
In France, according to a broad definition that is commonly accepted, « reuse » refers to the use of public data by third parties for purposes other than the public service mission for which the data was produced or received (this definition has been recalled in the legal guide provided by the French open data team : https://guides.data.gouv.fr/guides-open-data/guide-juridique/reutilisateurs-de-donnees/respecter-les-conditions-de-reutilisation). This definition directly stems from the Code of Relations between the Public and the Administration : « Public information contained in documents communicated or published by the administrations mentioned in the first paragraph of documents communicated or published by the administrations mentioned in the first paragraph of article L.300-2 may be used by any person who wishes to do so for purposes other than those of the public service mission for which the documents were produced or received. » (https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000033219044)

This definition is similar to the PSI Directive definition : « Public sector bodies collect, produce, reproduce and disseminate documents in order to fulfill their public service mission. The use of these documents for other purposes constitutes reuse ».

The complexity and the need to clarify the definition of reuse has been emphasised in the literature, particularly with respect to research data, a key issue being the distinction between use and reuse. Besides that definition, more restrictive approaches have also emerged : some consider that only perennial uses of data are reuses while others consider any use of data as reuse. In our day to day operations, any exploitation of data in order to obtain information is considered as reuse, whether this exploitation is freely accessible or not : following that definition, a use of private data or a data journalist’s work to prepare for an investigation will be considered as reuse.
